claims.text: The nanoparticles are equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, corresponding to approximately 20 at.% of each element.
The CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles are synthesized by inert gas condensation.
As-synthesized CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles form a near-random solid solution.
A random equiatomic atomic configuration maximizes configurational entropy.
Greater atomic randomness delays premelting relative to detectable short-range ordering or local clustering.
Greater atomic randomness elevates the overall melting temperature relative to short-range-ordered nanoparticles.
Local clusters act as nucleation sites for premelting.
Rapid quenching preserves a high degree of atomic randomness in CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles.
Slow annealing promotes local ordering or clustering in CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles.
High configurational entropy stabilizes the solid-solution phase.
A highly random configuration eliminates potential nucleation sites for premelting.
Clustering-induced lattice distortions locally lower the energy barrier and initiate premelting.
Rapidly quenched nanoparticles will have a sharper melting transition than slowly annealed nanoparticles.
Rapidly quenched nanoparticles will melt at a higher temperature than slowly annealed nanoparticles.
Slowly annealed nanoparticles will exhibit an earlier onset of premelting due to local clustering.
Rapidly quenched nanoparticles have minimal short-range order and greater thermal stability.
The proposed relationship should hold across a range of nanoparticle sizes and typical HEA compositions whenever the material remains a near-random solid solution.

contradictions.description: The intervention and falsification design describe quenching or annealing as pretreatments applied before DSC, whereas the conditions field says both sets are first heated beyond melting and that the differing cooling regimes are applied post-heating. This makes the timing of the ordering intervention relative to measurement internally inconsistent.
